audit_findings.title: Unreserved wage-and-hour class-action claims may rank ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduces the cash bridge for damages and penalties; any required prospective interview compensation also reduces recurring owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: At this stage of the litigation, it is not feasible to predict the outcome of or a range of loss, should a loss occur, from this proceeding and, accordingly, no amounts have been provided in the Company’s Financial Statements.
audit_findings.explanation: This is no longer merely a possible Gentry liability. The 2026 10-Q reports that the court found the Company liable for unpaid wages, liquidated damages and some PAGA penalties, although damages remain unquantified and no amount is accrued. Dorff remains unresolved, but class certification was denied. The established Gentry liability could be significant relative to $118.8 million of anchor owner earnings and the $324.714 million cash bridge, so the current valuation may overstate common-equity value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the damages-phase record, class-member and interview-hour data, penalty calculations, insurance coverage and any settlement or accrual; rerun the bridge for the uninsured liability and OE for any recurring interview-pay requirement.

audit_findings.title: The DCF projects a business the filing says cannot be reliably extrapolated
audit_findings.magnitude: Owner earnings declined $588.8 million, or 83.2%, from $707.6 million in 2022 to $118.8 million in 2025; terminal value represents 46.3%-51.5% of operating value and the scenario spread is $6.72 per share.
audit_findings.mechanism: Affects projected owner-earnings growth, margin recovery and terminal value rather than the historical OE calculation or balance-sheet bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Because long-term contracts are not a significant part of the Company’s business, future results cannot be reliably predicted by considering past trends or extrapolating past results.
audit_findings.explanation: The too-hard flag identifies the forecasting problem but does not resolve it: all reported values still depend on compounding OE and assigning a terminal value. With limited contractual visibility, large historical reversals and roughly half of operating value coming from the terminal calculation, unsupported growth paths are reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion in either direction.
audit_findings.action: Build each scenario from filed or contemporaneous bookings, hours, placements, rates, utilization and segment-margin evidence, then rerun the DCF with explicitly supported revenue and margin paths plus a no-recovery or runoff case.

audit_findings.title: The latest-quarter deferred-compensation offset was not verified
audit_findings.magnitude: At June 30, 2026, trust assets were $850.559 million versus $827.338 million of obligations, a $23.221 million surplus; $0 of trust assets is included in the $324.714 million cash bridge.
audit_findings.mechanism: Would affect the equity bridge only if plan obligations exceeded segregated trust assets or restricted trust assets were included as distributable cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company holds these assets to satisfy the Company’s liabilities under its deferred compensation plans.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied 2026 10-Q resolves the parsing uncertainty. It separately reports the trust assets and obligations, shows assets exceeding obligations, and reports cash and cash equivalents as a distinct $324.714 million line. Therefore, there is no demonstrated funding deficit or restricted-cash inclusion requiring a valuation adjustment.
audit_findings.action: No rerun is needed; continue keeping trust assets outside distributable cash and recheck the asset-liability offset in subsequent filings.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to treat all cash as excess
audit_findings.magnitude: $324.714 million bridge addition at risk, equal to $3.10 per diluted share and 14.2%-20.4% of reported scenario equity value; the actual operating-cash requirement is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash required for payroll, benefits, collateral and collection-cycle working capital should remain with operations rather than be added to the equity bridge as excess cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s working capital as of December 31, 2025, included $464 million in cash and cash equivalents and $748 million in net accounts receivable, both of which will be a significant source of ongoing liquidity and financial resilience.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing expressly describes cash and receivables as sources of ongoing liquidity, while first-half 2026 operations used $3.641 million of cash and accounts receivable increased by $78.943 million. This does not prove that all cash is operating, but it demonstrates that adding the entire balance without a minimum-cash analysis can materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Calculate minimum cash from weekly payroll and benefit disbursements, receivable collection timing, the $10.3 million of letters of credit, contractual commitments and stress-period liquidity; rerun every scenario adding only cash demonstrably exceeding that requirement.

audit_findings.title: The share ceiling may double-count issued restricted stock
audit_findings.magnitude: The disclosed outstanding award inventory was 1.994 million shares or units at December 31, 2025, equal to 1.9% of the 104.904453 million-share valuation denominator; removing all 1.994 million would raise base value only from $19.01 to approximately $19.38 per share.
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially inflates fully diluted shares by adding restricted shares already included in issued-and-outstanding common stock, thereby understating value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Recipients of restricted stock do not pay any cash consideration to the Company for the shares and have the right to vote all shares subject to such grant.
audit_findings.explanation: The denominator composition remains unreconciled, but even treating the entire disclosed 1.994 million award inventory as duplicated changes per-share value by only about 1.9%. The corrected base value would remain far below the $42.58 market price, so the maximum identifiable effect cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the July 31, 2026 transfer-agent count of 102.361828 million shares to issued restricted stock, unissued units and incremental performance-award payouts; correct the denominator if duplication is confirmed.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter overlooks partial-year acquisitions
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.722 million of acquisition cash payments, $2.685 million of contingent consideration and $12.418 million of recognized goodwill; acquired owner earnings and recurring investment needs are unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: A perimeter adjustment could increase anchor OE for the missing pre-acquisition months, while integration costs and recurring capital or working-capital needs could reduce it.
audit_findings.evidence: In April 2025, the Company expanded its operations through two acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisitions occurred in April 2025, so FY2025 contains only about nine months of their operations. Their disclosed transaction amounts are small relative to scenario equity values, but the filing does not disclose acquired revenue, earnings or investment requirements. The record therefore cannot establish whether the omitted run-rate is material or even its net direction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain acquisition-date financials or management disclosures for acquired revenue, operating profit, taxes, maintenance investment, working capital and integration costs; calculate twelve-month owner earnings and rerun the anchor only if the resulting perimeter adjustment is consequential.
